Spiral Detail organic form, earthy texture

A flowing curve meets a rugged, stone-like surface. Light traces the rounded spiral, picking out tiny pits and raised grains, while deep shadows draw the eye towards its centre.

The muted, earthy tones give this relief a fossil-like quality suggesting something shaped slowly by nature. Seen close up, its irregularities become as compelling as the larger form: rough edges, textured hollows and a continuous line that holds them all together.

Icarus - Illuminated Sculptural Wall Installation

Created for a private residence in Kensington, London, Icarus brings together a large hand-modelled wall relief with nine individually proportioned companion panels.

The central sculpture measuring approximately 2 × 1 metres carries an abstract language of incised lines, fractured shapes and gestural markings. The surface suggests fragments of wings, maps, architectural traces or half-remembered signs, reflecting the ideas of movement, aspiration and vulnerability associated with the story of Icarus.

Each panel is mounted proud of the wall and illuminated from behind. Concealed LED lighting creates a warm halo around the forms, transforming the installation as daylight fades and making the panels appear to float across the architectural surface.

The project was developed from sculpture and surface-making through to the practical engineering of the final installation. Custom stainless-steel structures were incorporated into the backs of the panels to support the works and accommodate the lighting system.

A bespoke Boldstone commission in which sculpture, light and architecture become a single composition.

A vertical study in rhythm, balance and repetition. Hand-shaped, elongated forms expand gradually towards the centre before contracting again, creating a quiet visual pulse across the surface.

The repeated forms might suggest stacked stones, seeds, fragments of an ancient language, musical notation or the measured pattern of breathing. Their arrangement is orderly without being uniform, allowing each element to retain its own subtle character.

Layers of verdigris, mineral green and weathered bronze tones give the relief a sense of age and discovery. As daylight moves across the raised surface, shifting shadows reveal its texture and changing depth.

Slender in proportion yet strongly architectural, the sculpture can be displayed as an individual statement piece or incorporated into a larger grouping.

Handmade by Boldstone. Each surface is individually created and no two finishes are ever exactly alike.

Riyadh Palace Pool

A site-specific series of large-scale architectural reliefs created for the swimming-pool courtyard of a private palace in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

The installation surrounds the water with a continuous sequence of sculptural panels, combining flowing striations, concentric arcs and spiral forms. Although each relief has its own composition, the repeated curves establish a unified rhythm around the courtyard, echoing waves, currents and the movement of water.

Integrated architectural lighting grazes the raised surfaces from below, intensifying the depth of the reliefs and producing strong bands of light and shadow. Reflections across the pool extend the sculpture into the surrounding space, transforming the installation after dark.

The studio photograph documents the fabrication stage before transport and installation, showing the scale of the individual panels and the range of interconnected designs developed for the commission.

Blue Tides Marbled Wall Panel Pair

Two slender wall panels exploring the contrasting movements of water.

The first composition is energetic and fragmented, with layers of cobalt, blue, ivory and black breaking across the surface like reflected light, fractured stone or waves seen from above. Beside it, the second panel moves in broader, more fluid currents, its sweeping bands folding and unfolding through the composition.

Together, the panels create a conversation between turbulence and calm between water in motion and the slower rhythms of tide, erosion and geological formation.

Their elongated proportions draw the eye upwards, making them particularly suited to narrow architectural spaces, entrance halls, stairways or rooms where a strong vertical element is required. Within this light-filled coastal interior, the blue marbled surfaces echo the surrounding sea and sky without becoming a literal landscape.

Handmade by Boldstone, with each marbled pattern formed individually so that no two surfaces can ever be exactly alike.
